summary: Describes how to use the Gandalf FZA data compression algorithm to squeeze PPP packets so they take less room on a link. It is an informational description of a vendor's compression scheme, not a standard.

plainLanguage.summary: It is like vacuum-packing your clothes before putting them into a suitcase. The same stuff takes up less room, so more fits through the link.

questions: how does fza compress ppp packets
subtitle: A compression algorithm for PPP links using the Gandalf FZA method.

tldr.problem: Point-to-point links have limited bandwidth, and PPP packets can be large. Compressing the packets saves bandwidth and improves throughput on these links.
tldr.mechanism: Gandalf FZA is a compression algorithm based on the LZ (Lempel-Ziv) method that maximizes compression at the expense of memory and CPU. PPP packets are compressed before transmission and decompressed on arrival, negotiated through the PPP Compression Control Protocol.
tldr.outcome: Compressed packets fit more data through a link, improving performance on bandwidth-limited connections. The scheme requires reliable in-order delivery, which PPP provides.

today: RFC 1993 is an Informational document describing a vendor-specific compression algorithm from Gandalf Data Limited. It documents how to use Gandalf FZA compression over PPP links through the Compression Control Protocol. Like other vendor-specific compression schemes, FZA saw limited adoption as PPP usage itself declined with broadband deployment.

sections.title: Introduction to Gandalf FZA Compression
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) provides a standard method for transporting datagrams over point-to-point links, and the PPP Compression Control Protocol (CCP) provides a method to negotiate and use compression algorithms. RFC 1993 describes the use of the Gandalf FZA data compression algorithm for compressing PPP encapsulated packets.

FZA is a high-performance derivative of the Lempel-Ziv (LZ) compression method. It maximizes compression ratio at the expense of CPU and memory consumption. Compression performance can be adjusted based on available resources. Licensing is available on a non-discriminatory basis.
sections.plainLanguage: Gandalf FZA is a way to make PPP data smaller before sending it across a slow link. The compression can be adjusted depending on how much memory and processing power you have.

sections.title: Packet Format and Requirements
sections.content:
Before any FZA packets are sent, PPP must reach the Network-Layer Protocol phase and the Compression Control Protocol (CCP) must have reached the Opened state with FZA negotiated as the primary compression algorithm. PPP Protocol field type hex 00FB is used for link compressed datagrams (outside multilink), and type hex 00FD is used for compressed datagrams (inside multilink or without multilink).

FZA packets consist of a PPP Protocol field (one or two octets) followed by compressed data. The maximum length is the same as a normal PPP Information field. Multiple PPP packets can be combined into a single compressed frame, or a single PPP packet can be split across multiple frames. FZA requires self-describing padding negotiation and a reliable, in-order delivery link.
sections.plainLanguage: Compressed packets get a type label (00FB or 00FD) so the other end knows they are compressed. Multiple packets can be combined or one packet can span several frames.

sections.title: Compression Characteristics and Data Expansion
sections.content:
The maximum expansion of Gandalf FZA is 2:1, meaning in the worst case expanded data is twice the original size. However, typical expansion on pre-compressed data is only 1.01:1, meaning compression schemes rarely cause significant bloat. When expansion exceeds the Maximum Receive Unit (MRU) for the link, the expanded packet is sent across multiple PPP frames with an indication in the compressed data marking the end of the original packet.

Expanded data is sent to maintain the integrity of the compression history. PPP Link Control Protocol packets MUST NOT be sent within compressed data, ensuring that control traffic is not affected by compression.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes already-compressed files don't compress well, and can actually get bigger. The algorithm handles this by either sending expanded data or splitting it across frames.

sections.title: Configuration and Negotiation
sections.content:
The CCP Gandalf-FZA Configuration Option is used to negotiate compression on the link. The option includes a Type field (value 19), a Length field (>= 3), a History field (one octet specifying the maximum compression history size in powers of 2, valid values 12 to 15), and an optional Version field.

The Version field is not present for standard FZA, but contains the value 1 for FZA+, an improved variant. By default or if negotiation fails, no compression is used. The peer is not required to send as many histories as the implementation indicates it can accept.
sections.plainLanguage: Before sending compressed data, the two ends agree on how much history to keep (which affects compression strength) and which FZA version to use (FZA or FZA+).

fields.name: PPP Protocol
fields.desc: Type hex 00FB (link compressed) or 00FD (compressed). May be compressed with LCP Protocol-Field-Compression.

fields.name: Compressed Data
fields.desc: One or more octets of FZA-compressed PPP packets with original protocol number and information field.
